neighbours.label: language that sorts people or things into separate groups or categories (segregation, divided along lines, sorted into separate tracks, into different bins), as against putting the same things together
fire: In the old factory town, workers were housed in segregated districts by trade.
The museum arranges its fossils into separate rooms according to their age.
Teachers once streamed pupils into different classes based on a single test.
The warehouse staff sort the parcels into distinct piles for each city.
For decades the island was split along sharp religious divisions.
The survey classifies the plants into three categories by leaf shape.
At the clinic, patients are separated into groups according to their symptoms.
The coach divided the players into two teams by their age.
quiet: In the old factory town, workers lived together in a few narrow streets.
The museum shows all of its fossils in one large room near the entrance.
Teachers once taught every pupil in the same class, whatever their age.
The warehouse staff load the parcels onto one truck every morning.
For decades the island was known for its quiet harbours and fishing.
The survey counts the plants in every field along the river.
At the clinic, patients wait together in a bright room with magazines.
The coach gathered all the players together for a talk after the match.
